style_variants: environmental panorama to hotspot; plant/rhizosphere to mechanistic inset
recommended_usage: Use when mechanism depends on a spatial niche or environmental interface
avoid_usage: Do not let contextual scenery overpower the mechanism
notes: Strong bridge from ecological context to molecular/cellular process

style_variants: band diagram; potential ladder; redox ruler
recommended_usage: Use to justify feasibility or energy direction without a separate full panel
avoid_usage: Avoid tiny labels and too many competing energy conventions
notes: Works best as a narrow side module

style_variants: day/night aerobic-anoxic; low/high Fe condition
recommended_usage: Use for perturbation comparisons with matched visual grammar
avoid_usage: Avoid changing too many unrelated visual variables between sides
notes: Central transition cue should make comparison explicit

style_variants: large circular two-state arrow
recommended_usage: Use when two regimes alternate or interconvert
avoid_usage: Avoid if conditions are independent rather than cyclic
notes: Good for oxygen or temporal-switch perturbations

style_variants: plant scene plus rounded mechanistic inset
recommended_usage: Use when root/mineral/microbe localization matters
avoid_usage: Avoid excessive root-detail if the biological interface is the true focus
notes: Natural context can remain low-saturation while mechanism uses accent colors

style_variants: rounded translucent cell capsule; clustered rods on material; soft donor/recipient cells
recommended_usage: Use for accessible interface/phenotype mechanisms where volume helps separate objects
avoid_usage: Avoid strong glow and decorative depth at small journal scale
notes: Best when depth clarifies contact, not when it is purely decorative

style_variants: methanotroph membrane-to-metabolism; outer/periplasmic/cytosolic layered membrane
recommended_usage: Use for EET/EEU, transporter, respiratory-chain and methane-oxidation mechanisms
avoid_usage: Avoid overpopulating every membrane protein with equal visual weight
notes: Compartment labels should anchor the reading order

style_variants: dark bead chain crossing periplasm
recommended_usage: Use for conductive mineral/protein bridge hypotheses
avoid_usage: Avoid making a candidate bridge look established without visual qualification
notes: Distinct geometry makes conductive route legible

style_variants: yellow photoelectron; red e-; blue alternative route; charge/discharge loop
recommended_usage: Reserve a consistent accent color and explicit e- semantics
avoid_usage: Avoid reusing the same color for carbon or generic causality
notes: Electron grammar should be globally consistent within one figure

style_variants: dashed arrow/line for putative route
recommended_usage: Use to distinguish proposed from established mechanisms
avoid_usage: Avoid mixing dashed lines for purely spatial grouping
notes: Useful for evidence-boundary discipline

style_variants: left synthesis module to right functional EET module
recommended_usage: Use when material formation and downstream function are distinct stages
avoid_usage: Avoid a severe density imbalance between the two halves
notes: A strong bridge arrow can encode stage transition

style_variants: small explanatory modules above a large integrated mechanism
recommended_usage: Use when a biohybrid contains unfamiliar chemistry that needs pre-explanation
avoid_usage: Avoid repeating the same content in all panels
notes: Particularly strong for Bath-Bio-Se / light-driven EEU concepts

style_variants: warm yellow light field around cell
recommended_usage: Use to encode photoactivation without complex optics
avoid_usage: Avoid treating glow as decorative if light is not mechanistically relevant
notes: Keep saturation restrained to preserve scientific tone

style_variants: electron/hole, pathway, regulatory and elemental process accents
recommended_usage: Use a small number of semantic accent colors
avoid_usage: Avoid rainbow coding and unlabelled color meaning
notes: Color should reinforce arrow semantics and hierarchy

style_variants: large mechanism plus compact evidence dashboard
recommended_usage: Use when one mechanism is the conceptual anchor and several data modules are supportive
avoid_usage: Avoid making every small evidence panel equally prominent
notes: Good bridge from mechanism to transcript/validation evidence

style_variants: central electrode/material object with numbered zoom bubbles
recommended_usage: Use when one interface supports several mechanistic interaction modes
avoid_usage: Avoid more than three or four equal-weight callouts
notes: Strong for GAC, electrode and mineral–microbe interface figures

style_variants: central interface branching to multiple application boxes
recommended_usage: Use in graphical abstracts that connect mechanism to function/application
avoid_usage: Avoid if the applications are not central to the scientific story
notes: Keep application arrows visually distinct from electron arrows

style_variants: warm productive route versus cool alternative/no-DIET route
recommended_usage: Use to compare competing interspecies electron-transfer interpretations
avoid_usage: Avoid implying certainty through saturated color alone
notes: Pair color with explicit route labels or line-style qualifiers

style_variants: quantitative panel above compact interpretation schematic
recommended_usage: Use when one result directly motivates a mechanistic explanation
avoid_usage: Avoid allowing the schematic to visually outrank the evidence
notes: Strong for perturbation and redox-storage narratives

style_variants: paired organisms around a central reversible Fe redox/storage loop
recommended_usage: Use for charge/discharge or mediator-storage concepts
avoid_usage: Avoid battery metaphors when no reversible storage exists
notes: Circular geometry makes temporal cycling immediately legible

style_variants: environmental context → protective response → survival/death
recommended_usage: Use for compact stress/phenotype graphical abstracts
avoid_usage: Avoid clip-art literalism and excessive text inside icons
notes: Best at low-to-medium information density

style_variants: circular heatmaps + grouped bars + large synthesis mechanism
recommended_usage: Use when omics evidence must visibly converge on one model
avoid_usage: Avoid for standalone mechanisms or slide figures with limited space
notes: Primarily a composition/information-hierarchy reference; overlaps with BI019

style_variants: matched biotic/abiotic mechanisms stacked vertically
recommended_usage: Use to compare causal alternatives while holding geometry constant
avoid_usage: Avoid changing organism positions or scale between conditions
notes: Shared geometry makes the altered arrows carry the contrast

style_variants: top gas/membrane oxidation → central carbon node → lower assimilation/fermentation branches
recommended_usage: Use for Bath metabolism, oxygen effects and carbon/electron allocation
avoid_usage: Avoid full genome-scale enzyme density
notes: Especially strong for linking methane oxidation to downstream carbon fate
